messages:
maria: FYI — we flipped the org-wide audit log retention from 90d -> 365d in eu-west last night. noticed a spike in provisioning latency for GPU pools this morning, several nodes failing to join the cluster.
alex: saw that. getting multiple timeouts from keystore decrypt calls during node bootstrap. suspect larger TLS session table / NAT gateway pressure from increased log uploads.
jae: @maria can you paste the retention rollout PR? curious if it changed the S3 lifecycle or KMS key usage patterns.
maria: https://redwood.internal/r/pr/4521 — retention change + consolidated delivery to the central logging bucket. KMS key is the same but we enabled request logging for the delivery role.
sre-sam: ops-bot alerted: "node-group/eu-west-gpu-* failed 8/12 bootstrap steps: keystore decrypt error, iam:AssumeRole failure" — logs attached in the alert.
ops-bot: Automated: incident created #inc-21876, severity P2, assigned to eng-platform.
security-liz: initial suspicion: role chaining. If the delivery principal started signing more requests or rotated role session tags, STS throttling could surface. Also verify that firewall rules to logging collectors didn't change and overflowed conntrack.
infra-nik: I've tail'd the node-init log; the error is: `error decrypting key: AccessDenied` but IAM trace shows `sts:AssumeRole` returning 429 for the delivery role for bursts.
alex: 429 on STS + increased S3 PutObject throughput => we might be hitting a global service quota or hitting per-account STS throttling due to many long-lived sessions from the logging pipeline.
jae: quick mitigation: reduce simultaneous log upload parallelism and pin a local cache for keystore responses during bootstrap. Pushing a small patch to node-init to backoff on decrypt and fallback to cached key when available.
maria: I'm rolling back the consolidated delivery config to keep per-region buckets for now — that should reduce cross-region egress and flatten KMS usage.
security-liz: also recommend adding a firewall rule to limit connections from the logging agents to the collector to a token-based proxy so we don't DOS STS with unauthenticated retries.
alex: adding here the IAM trust snippet we saw that could cause token churn:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::999999:role/logging-delivery"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole","Condition":{"NumericLessThan":{"aws:MultiFactorAuthAge":"300"}}}
  ]
}
```
infra-nik: that Condition forces short sessions — combined with aggressive retry it explodes STS calls. we should remove the MFA age condition for machine roles.
sre-sam: actions: 1) maria revert consolidated delivery (in progress), 2) jae push node-init backoff patch (PR 7591), 3) security-liz to review role trust conditions and propose conservative session TTL, 4) infra-nik to add local keystore caching for bootstrap token reuse.
maria: revert deployed to eu-west buckets at 08:12 UTC. initial signs: 40% reduction in STS errors, node join rate recovering.
ops-bot: Automated: alert resolved #inc-21876 — metric STS 429s returned to baseline.
security-liz: follow-up backlog item: audit the other regions for similar trust-condition patterns and add quota alarms for STS and S3 PutObject QPS before next retention change.
alex: noted — I'll open a tracking ticket with cost estimate for per-region vs consolidated delivery (network egress + KMS requests). leaning to keep per-region buckets + cross-region lifecycle jobs during low-load windows.
maria: thanks everyone. will schedule a postmortem doc and include the patch links + runbook updates. cc: @sre-sam for OPS runbook edits."
